name: NuoDB
tagline: Elastic distributed SQL with in-memory transaction engines and separate storage managers, owned by Dassault.
description: NuoDB is a distributed SQL database built around a two-tier, peer-to-peer design: Transaction Engines are in-memory SQL processes that cache data on demand, while Storage Managers persist it, and either tier can be scaled out independently. That makes it good at elastic scale-out of SQL compute and continuous availability across nodes and data centers, while keeping ACID semantics through MVCC. Dassault Systèmes acquired the company in 2020 and now develops it largely as infrastructure for its 3DEXPERIENCE platform, while still selling it with Kubernetes Helm charts and a DBaaS control plane. It is a niche choice today, mostly relevant to existing customers.

pricing.notes: Sold under enterprise agreements; historically offered a limited free Community Edition.

scale.notes: Transaction Engines and Storage Managers scale independently; multiple Storage Managers can run in different data centers.

strengths: SQL compute (Transaction Engines) scales out independently from storage
Peer-to-peer design with no single coordinator to fail
ACID transactions with MVCC across nodes
Official Helm charts for Kubernetes deployment
weaknesses: Small user community and few third-party integrations
Product direction driven by Dassault's internal needs
No public pricing or free tier today
Lacks modern features such as JSON, vector or CDC tooling found in competitors
useCases: Existing NuoDB deployments in financial services and ISVs
notIdealFor: Greenfield projects wanting an active open ecosystem
Teams wanting a managed cloud service
